claims.claim: Melting CuBr, BiBr3 and Bi(2)Q(3) (Q=S or Se) yields black needles of quaternary chalcogenide bromides.
claims.quote: Melting reactions of CuBr, BiBr3 and Bi(2)Q(3) (Q = S or Se) resulted in black needles of quaternary chalcogenide bromides.

claims.claim: Cu1.5Bi2.64S3.42Br2.58 crystallizes in monoclinic C2/m at 293(2) K; the selenide Cu1.57Bi2.37Se2.68Br3.32 is isostructural.
claims.quote: Cu1.5Bi2.64S3.42Br2.58 has a melting point of 708(5) K and crystallizes in the monoclinic space group C2/m with a = 1315.1(3) pm, b = 410.28(5) pm, c = 937.2(2) pm, beta = 90.33(2)degrees at T = 293(2) K. The isostructural selenide Cu1.57Bi2.37Se2.68Br3.32, which melts at 724(5) K, has the lattice parameters a = 1353.9(3) pm, b = 417.54(5) pm, c = 960.4(2) pm, beta = 91.13(2)degrees.

claims.claim: Chemical vapor transport of CuI and Bi2Se3 yields black needles of Cu1.57Bi4.69Se7.64I0.36 and Cu2.31Bi5Se8.31I0.69.
claims.quote: Black needles of the selenide iodides Cu1.57Bi4.69Se7.64I0.36 and Cu2.31Bi5Se8.31I0.69 were obtained by chemical vapor transport of CuI and Bi2Se3.

claims.claim: Both selenide iodides crystallize in C2/m.
claims.quote: They also crystallize in space group type C2/m with a = 1373.9(4) pm, b = 417.4(1) pm, c = 1464.6(4) pm, beta = 115.57(2)degrees, and a = 1369.1(3) pm, b = 416.6(1) pm, c = 1526.4(3) pm, beta = 99.81(3)degrees, respectively.

claims.claim: All four pavonite homologous compounds have alternating layered modules A and B parallel to (001).
claims.quote: All four compounds belong to pavonite homologous series. Their structures are built up of two alternating types of layered modules parallel (001), denoted A and B.

claims.claim: Module A has almost the same composition and shape across the structures: paired rods along [010] and copper(I) distributed in voids between them.
claims.quote: Composition and shape of module A are almost the same in all structures. They consist of paired rods (1)(infinity)[BiQ(3/3)X(2/2)Z(2/2)] (Z = Q/X; X = Br, I) running along [010] and copper(I) cations that are distributed over various voids between the rods.

claims.claim: Module B comprises [MZ(6)] octahedra (M=Bi/Cu) arranged in NaCl-type fragments of thickness N=1, 3 or 4.
claims.quote: Modules of type B are composed of [MZ(6)] octahedra (M = Bi/Cu), which are arranged in NaCl-type fragments of thickness N = 1, 3 or 4.

claims.claim: JPDF reveals a continuous copper-ion transport pathway along [010] in the sulfide bromide.
claims.quote: The Joint Probability Density Function (JPDF) reveals a continuous pathway for copper ion transport along [010] in the case of the sulfide bromide.

claims.claim: The copper-ion hopping pseudo-potential is calculated as 47 meV.
claims.quote: The pseudo-potential for hopping of copper ions was calculated as 47 meV only.

claims.claim: The physically cross-linked PAA/PEO network doped with NaCl has breaking stress >1.3 MPa, stretchability >1100%, and toughness up to 7.34 MJ m(-3).
claims.quote: Composed of a physically cross-linked network of polyacrylic acid (PAA) and polyethylene glycol (PEO) doped with sodium chloride, the resulting PAA-PEO-NaCl ionic hydrogels demonstrates impressive mechanical strength (breaking stress >1.3 MPa), stretchability (>1100%), and toughness (up to 7.34 MJ m(-3)).

claims.claim: Reversible hydrogen bonding and chain entanglement jointly impart mechanical resilience, adhesion, and self-healing to the hydrogels.
claims.quote: Moreover, the reversible hydrogen bonding interaction and chain entanglement render the ionic hydrogels with excellent mechanical resilience, adhesion properties, and self-healing properties.

claims.claim: At ambient conditions, the damaged hydrogels immediately recover electrochemical and thermoelectric performance; mechanical healing is complete within 24 h.
claims.quote: At ambient conditions, the electrochemical and thermoelectric performance of the ionic hydrogels can be restored immediately from physical damage such as cutting, and the mechanical healing can be completely restored within 24 h.

claims.claim: At optimized composition, the hydrogels reach Seebeck coefficient 3.26 mV K-1 and thermal conductivity 0.321 W m(-1) K-1.
claims.quote: At the optimized composition, the Seebeck coefficient of the ionic hydrogels can reach 3.26 mV K-1 with a low thermal conductivity of 0.321 W m(-1) K-1.

claims.claim: Authors propose that combined mechanical and thermoelectric performance makes these hydrogels applicable in ionic thermoelectric capacitors converting low-grade heat for soft electronics; this is a proposed application.
claims.quote: Considering the excellent mechanical properties and thermoelectric performance, it is believed that the ionic hydrogels are widely applicable in ionic thermoelectric capacitors to convert low-grade heat into electricity for soft electronic devices.

claims.claim: Seebeck coefficients from the reported Cu-CuSO4 experiments fit the characteristic model extracted from deBethune et al. (1959).
claims.quote: Some limited new experimental data on power generation for the underdeveloped Cu-CuSO4 system are also reported. The Seebeck coefficient values of these experiments fit with a characteristic model extracted from a 1959 paper by deBethune et al. (Journal of the Electrochemical Society, Vol. 106, 1959).

claims.claim: Gelatin/kappa-carrageenan ionic hydrogel meets flow, recovery, and structural requirements for multi-material direct ink writing.
claims.quote: Here, we present a 3D-printable ionic hydrogel based on a gelatin and kappa-carrageenan matrix that meets the flow, recovery, and structural requirements of multi-material direct ink writing.

claims.claim: Kappa-carrageenan modulates precursor viscoelasticity in the gelatin/kappa-carrageenan ink.
claims.quote: Our ink design consists of gelatin and kappa-carrageenan, where the latter modulates the viscoelasticity of the precursor and enables the formation of a double-network porous structure, thereby enhancing mechanical robustness and facilitating ion transport.

claims.claim: Kappa-carrageenan enables a double-network porous structure in the ink.
claims.quote: Our ink design consists of gelatin and kappa-carrageenan, where the latter modulates the viscoelasticity of the precursor and enables the formation of a double-network porous structure, thereby enhancing mechanical robustness and facilitating ion transport.

claims.claim: Formation of the double-network porous structure enhances mechanical robustness.
claims.quote: Our ink design consists of gelatin and kappa-carrageenan, where the latter modulates the viscoelasticity of the precursor and enables the formation of a double-network porous structure, thereby enhancing mechanical robustness and facilitating ion transport.

claims.claim: Formation of the double-network porous structure facilitates ion transport.
claims.quote: Our ink design consists of gelatin and kappa-carrageenan, where the latter modulates the viscoelasticity of the precursor and enables the formation of a double-network porous structure, thereby enhancing mechanical robustness and facilitating ion transport.

claims.claim: In-situ silicone encapsulation suppresses dehydration and thereby extends operational lifetime.
claims.quote: High-fidelity 3D architectures can be printed, and an in-situ silicone encapsulation effectively suppresses dehydration, extending operational lifetime.

claims.claim: Geometry optimization such as wavy structures increases ion-migration pathways.
claims.quote: Geometry-optimised features such as wavy structures further improve strain responsiveness by increasing ion-migration pathways.

claims.claim: Increasing ion-migration pathways mediates improved strain responsiveness of geometry-optimized features such as wavy structures.
claims.quote: Geometry-optimised features such as wavy structures further improve strain responsiveness by increasing ion-migration pathways.

claims.claim: With the reported SO4/SO3 redox couple, hydrogel reaches Seebeck coefficient 3.96 mV K-1 and maintains stable thermoelectric output during deformation.
claims.quote: With an SO4 & sup2;(-)/SO3 & sup2;(-) redox couple, the hydrogel reaches a Seebeck coefficient of 3.96 mV K-& sup1; and maintains stable thermoelectric output during deformation.

claims.claim: Temperature sensing, motion detection, and encoded-signal demonstrations support this printing strategy for monolithic, long-lasting, form-adaptive self-powered wearables.
claims.quote: Demonstrations of temperature sensing, motion detection, and encoded signal output validate the capability of this integrated printing strategy to produce monolithic, long-lasting, and form-adaptive self-powered wearable devices.
